clue.text: Uncultured bishop breaking down chain

indicators.note: the bishop's letter breaks into the pair of words, sitting between them

parts.note: feeling down is feeling low
a chain of things in a line is a row
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A philistine cleric disrupts a chain of command or some sort of procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lowbrow has unsophisticated tastes, a synonym for uncultured.

clue.text: Fine fabric of Nice, all cut short

indicators.note: each of the three words is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric
taken as written
taken as written
the last letter of the word for fine fabric is the one cut
the last letter of of is the one cut
the last letter of Nice is the one cut

explanation.surface: Delicate material from Nice is trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all cut' removes the last letter of LACE, OF and NICE, giving LAC + O + NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is brief and terse, using few words.

clue.text: Blow aimed at stunning someone

parts.note: not a punch to knock someone out but a blast of breath directed at an attractive person, a stunner

explanation.definitionFit: A wolf whistle is a whistle blown at an attractive person, a stunner.

clue.text: Live turn by some in bed is erotic

indicators.note: the hidden letters turn round and read backwards
some of the letters inside the phrase are taken

explanation.surface: Living with someone means turning over in bed for something sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the run EDISER found inside 'bed is erotic'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live there.

clue.text: Polish car Lily crashed to get carried away

parts.note: to polish a car is to wax it

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: After polishing her car, Lily crashed it and was carried off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax lyrical is to talk with too much enthusiasm, getting carried away.

clue.text: Ancient Egyptian confused him with poet

indicators.note: letters that are confused are jumbled, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old Egyptian mixes up a man with a versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Imhotep was the architect and physician of ancient Egypt who designed the step pyramid at Saqqara.

clue.text: Fellow's cut key for Joanna

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano, whose keys were made of ivory

explanation.surface: A man has a key cut for a woman named Joanna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joanna' is not a woman but Cockney rhyming slang for piano; an ivory is a piano key.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor is a man's name, and fellow can mean a man.

clue.text: Jack keeps book in reserve for stamp collector, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for jack keeps the other pieces inside

parts.note: to jack something up is to hoist it
put by means set aside in reserve

explanation.surface: A man named Jack holds a book back for a philatelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name but is the verb hoist.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp collector is one example of someone who pursues a hobby.

clue.text: Leaves having packed one's bags?

parts.note: looks like someone departing with luggage, but the leaves are dried ones packed into little paper sachets

explanation.definitionFit: Tea leaves are packed into tea bags for brewing.

clue.text: Parking on sharp double bends: that is a gift!

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
re means on or concerning

indicators.note: a sharp double bend is two tight turns in a row, so the bend letter is written twice

parts.note: a Z is shaped like a sharp bend in the road, as on warning signs
ie abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Getting a parking spot on a twisty road is a stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gift!' looks like praise for easy parking, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A prezzie is informal British slang for a present.

clue.text: Mustard dip?

definitions.meaning: Colonel Mustard is a suspect in the board game Cluedo, and colonel is abbreviated to three letters
a dip or saddle between two mountain peaks

explanation.walkthrough: Mustard is the Cluedo character Colonel Mustard, whose rank shortens to three letters; the condiment reading is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a low pass in a ridge, and the abbreviation is the rank of the Cluedo colonel.

clue.text: Female, say, to pay attention to mere detective

parts.note: female is an example of a sex
NB, nota bene, tells a reader to take note
a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: A woman is told to notice a mere detective, as if the sleuth were unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like 'only' qualifying the detective, but it is a noun meaning a lake. NB is Latin nota bene, 'note well'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexton Blake is a fictional British detective of story papers and pulp fiction.

clue.text: After objection, means to include small advertisement in our Times

indicators.note: the means and advertisement part follows the objection in the answer

parts.note: no is a word of objection

indicators.note: the word for means takes the advert inside it

parts.note: ways are means of doing something
ad is a short advertisement

explanation.surface: A complaint leads to a short advert being placed in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our Times' plays on the newspaper the clue appeared in; the definition means the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means at the present time, the times we live in.

clue.text: Central Asian finally took money for painting by Velasquez

indicators.note: finally applies to every following word, taking the closing letter of each

explanation.surface: Someone from Central Asia pays for a Velasquez canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' seems to attach only to 'took', but it takes the last letter of all six words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kyrgyz is a native of Kyrgyzstan in Central Asia.

clue.text: Creature that's large and grand bizarrely wandering around unknown

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the unknown

parts.note: G abbreviates grand, a thousand

indicators.note: letters wandering stray from their places, so these are shuffled

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns; here z

explanation.surface: Some big beast lumbers about in a strange way, far from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges G plus BIZARRELY, which then goes around Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A grizzly bear is a large North American bear, an animal of great size.

clue.text: Unlikely to meet Norm, Rod lounged about

parts.note: a pole is a rod

indicators.note: the word for lounged goes about the norm

parts.note: sat means lounged around
par is the norm or standard

explanation.surface: Norm and Rod sat lazing around, two men who never meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm' and 'Rod' look like men's names but are words for standard and pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Things poles apart are as far away as possible, so they never meet.

clue.text: Short film part for one that's the bulldog type?

definitions.meaning: a brief extract from a film

definitions.text: for one that's the bulldog type?
definitions.meaning: a bulldog is one kind of spring fastener for paper, the bulldog type being an example

explanation.definitionFit: A clip is an excerpt from a film, and also a fastener such as the bulldog variety.

clue.text: Poor contribution partner left to club

parts.note: a widow is the partner left after a spouse dies
to club is to strike, or smite

explanation.surface: A spouse abandons someone by walking out, then resorts to violence.
explanation.walkthrough: The widow's mite is the Gospel story of a poor widow's tiny offering, valued above rich gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: The widow's mite is a small offering from someone poor, a contribution that is little but generous.

clue.text: American creature caught greeting quietly spoken brother

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hi is a greeting
P is piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: spoken means the next word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a monk is a brother in a religious order

explanation.surface: An American animal was caught saying hello softly to a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipmunk is a small striped North American squirrel.

clue.text: After wind started, burning cloud left plant

indicators.note: the word wind is only started, giving its opening letter

parts.note: a burning sensation is an itch
a haze is a cloud of mist or smoke

explanation.surface: Once the wind got up, a smouldering fire's smoke left behind a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Witch hazel is a shrub whose bark gives an astringent lotion.

clue.text: Astrologers reversing downfall after final change of direction

indicators.note: the whole word reads backwards
the last letter, a compass point south, changes to another point, west

parts.note: nemesis is ruin or downfall

explanation.surface: Stargazers are reversing their decline after a last-minute U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final change of direction' changes NEMESIS's last S (south) to W (west), giving NEMESIW, which reversed gives WISEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wise Men or Magi of the Nativity story were astrologers who followed a star.

clue.text: Pound artillery with ersatz shell

indicators.note: a shell is the outside of something, here the outside letters of ersatz

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Fake shells are fired by artillery, measured in pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like a verb of bombardment, matching artillery and shell, but it is the American poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was the American modernist poet, so the first name fills in for the surname.

clue.text: Expert to make firm solvent

parts.note: an ace is an expert
to tone muscles is to firm them

explanation.surface: An expert firms up a solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvent' could mean financially sound, matching a firm, but it is the chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a common chemical solvent, used in nail varnish remover.

clue.text: Top EU broadcaster beset by worry

indicators.note: the broadcaster is surrounded by the word for worry

parts.note: to vex is to worry
RTE is the Irish state broadcaster, Ireland being in the EU

explanation.surface: The head of a European broadcaster is plagued by worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertex is the highest point or apex, the top.

clue.text: Quiet spot includes place to shelter

indicators.note: the word for spot takes the shelter inside it

parts.note: to spot is to spy
the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A quiet place has a sheltered corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepy village is quiet, with little activity.

clue.text: German certainly born year before English heroine

parts.note: ja is German for yes
nee marks a woman's maiden name, French for born

explanation.surface: A German, quite certain, was born a year before an English heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English heroine' reads as one phrase, but English gives only the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre is the heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel.

clue.text: Service centre one's pressed to close?

definitions.meaning: a ... farm is where stallions service mares
a press ... is a fastener pushed together to close

explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a breeding establishment and also a press-fastener for clothing.

clue.text: Timid chap quiet — almost unnaturally

indicators.note: arranged unnaturally, so the letters of the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A shy man is quiet, almost unnaturally so.
explanation.definitionFit: A milquetoast is a feeble, timid person, from the comic-strip character Caspar Milquetoast.

clue.text: Boy fast running out of time

indicators.note: the word runs out of the time letter, losing it

parts.note: Lent is the Christian fast

explanation.surface: A boy hurries off, out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast running' looks like speed, but fast is the noun Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard.

clue.text: I let gaol's odd characters escape

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters get away, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A prisoner admits letting oddballs break out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: From LETGAOL the odd-placed L, T, A, L escape; 'gaol' is British for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the I of a person.

clue.text: Cooking kind son's sticking in the pan?

indicators.note: cooking up something rearranges it, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A cook makes kind remarks about a son's food sticking in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The pan is a skid pan, a slippery track for practising car control, not a frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-skid tyres or surfaces grip rather than sliding, sticking even on a skid pan.

clue.text: Holding a vote, fine old actor relieved of all duties

indicators.note: the actor's name holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a Victorian actor-manager
X is the mark of a vote on a ballot
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A veteran actor taking part in a ballot is excused all his obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relieved of all duties' suggests someone sacked, but it means free of tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax-free goods carry no duty, so they are relieved of all duties.
